tips.comment: Sea Invasion has won here over hurdles 2m4f last year and fences CD (last time out). Both wins have been on good and looked as if there was more in the tank when winning that race 3 weeks ago.

The model I run simulates this race and suggests Arfursgal can win this one. Goes out with the highest RPR of the field and the joint lowest weight to carry. Previous good second and third and looks to go one better here for this 2m 1f National Hunt Flat.
Worth a look at this selection - yard has a good turn around in Bumpers and has breeding to suit. E/W shout on first outing in a field of limited form on offer.
Jaxonne, a CD winner on good at this time last year, showed strong signs of getting back to his best last time at Wincanton. If he builds on that a little today, then he should win this.
Improvement for the 3rd run this year when runner-up over further on similar ground as today's. The improvement could have come from the first wear of a hood, which is now retained.

The model I run suggests an upset from Bahtiyar. Admittedly, this output doesn't look convincing, but the result has been driven by this horse having the highest RPR of the field. Tabitha Worsley on board claims 3 lbs and has been in decent form. This horse has by far the highest top speed on the card.

The model suggests Luna Run can win the last race of the day. Luna Run has the highest RPR of the field but doesn't seem to be impacted by the weights. Goes out carrying the second lowest weight, with the lowest weight being the rank outsider at 80/1. #LunaRun is the only one to have won previously on this distance.

Big improver last year. Won his maiden on Tapeta, then followed up winning a similar race as today's and was then upped in grade and placed in a decent Class 2. Back down in grade today from the same mark as when last seen in October. Will go close if ready to rumble.

Won a maiden for Richard Hannon at Salisbury in May last year before running two below par races and ended up being sold (albeit to William Haggas which is an upgrade). He's had three runs for Haggas so far and he made his seasonal reappearance last time out at Ripon in a Class 2 when only 4th of 7 but it was a decent return and he was sent off 5/2 favourite. He should come on plenty for that run and Tom Marquand is now booked so i think he has a good chance on his AW debut if he enjoys the switch to this surface.

Steel Tiger is on a roll, coming into this off back-to-back wins, including a gutsy success at Chelmsford last time. He’s up 4lb but still looks fairly treated off 86, and with Harry Davies booked, he’s got a solid chance of landing the hat-trick.
More wins than places in the last 5 runs, mostly here at Newcastle. C&D winner, always shows up ready and willing, and has a proven record here - could have easily been my NAP.

SHERADANN holds a subsequent entry in a similarly competitive looking race. Trainer Ian Williams does well with the runners he sends long distances and taking in this slightly shorter than optimim trip as a fresh horse could work.. Noteworthy booking and a player.

I think HUMBLE SPARK is a cracking each way price here at 11/1 (4 places). Kildare Legend is in no way a good thing given his owner’s 0/6 record with favourites coming down in class, meanwhile Steel Tiger has to overcome H Davies’ 5% SR (A/E 0.31) in May on the AW. Sam Hawkens carries a poor FlatStats rating alongside Galileo’s 7% SR (A/E 0.45) with runners returning off 15 to 28 days away and Federated is taking a marked step up in class which I’m not convinced will suit. The I Williams yard are in an almighty slump (1/46, A/E 0.26 over the past month) which puts me off Sheradann but HS can be chanced dropping down in class after being badly hampered on the rails over 16.5f here at Newcastle last month. The son of Acclamation holds a healthy 30% SR (A/E 1.57) on the AW, 4 of which coming at this venue and the booking of P Mulrennan is a positive given his 25% SR (A/E 1.46) over the past fortnight and 33% SR (A/E 1.73) when riding for these owners. Their 46% SR (A/E 1.8) with 5yo’s over LD trips at Newcastle provides further optimism.

Looked like they did not see out the extended 2 miles here Lto and record over this C/D reads 2/1/1, so drop back in trip looks a plus. Is a little off putting that P. Mulrennan prefers another one in the race, but we have able deputy in J.Fanning and very good dual trainer who is in top form @ present, 16 percent with a Lsp of 18.88 on his 4yo plus last 5 seasons, making current 12/1 solid Ew value in the race.
Has been running consistently well on turf and is returning to the all-weather for the first time since 2021. Holds an each-way chance.
Gained valuable course experience in debut run back in 2021, but all 3 wins to date have been on turf. Can win off current mark and hoping the use of cheekpieces helps.

Orange Sky returns to Newcastle after a smooth course-and-distance win last September, where she justified favouritism with a 1½-length victory. She had previously finished second at Newbury, showing promise on debut. Now carrying a penalty, she faces a modest field and is expected to be a strong contender if she maintains her form.

Orange Sky makes the trip up from Newmarket for a seasonal return but carries a penalty and is weak in the market for an odds-on chance. Lorna B impressed when taking the scalp of another odds-on chance at this track in March over 6 furlongs. She is by a new season sire with a cheap stud fee, but his progeny have been winning all over the place in the last month. The step up to 7 furlongs will suit.

Wasn't beaten far on debut when finishing second over C&D in November last year but was well beaten over the same trip at Southwell last month when returning from five months off. Should be fitter today. Adam Farragher in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

Clearly not faniced in betting market on debut run and this showed in the race as they were very green in running, when coming 9/11 beaten 10 lengths in a class 4 novice over 6f @ Yarmouth. However, entitled to come on for that run/experience, step up to this 7f should suit on nice pedigree, good jockey up and very shrewd trainer who has done very well here last 5 seasons, 26 percent with his 3yo's in same period, making current 14/1 solid Ew value against the hot favourite.

Not much to go on and the market suggests she really has an uphill task to cause an upset tomorrow however the sire (Sergei Prokofiev (CAN)) just might be the key as in good form and in profit in the last 28 days, boasting a 68.3% ROI.

Still unexposed after only 4 career runs and he's won two of them to date at Haydock and Lingfield where winning by a nose, before following up and winning by 3 and a half lengths. His debut at Kempton also looks good form as he finished ahead of Storm Star that day who has since won three Class 2s on the bounce and is rated 100 with two Group 1 entries in the Lockinge and the Queen Anne, (1st and 2nd in that race ahead of him are rated 96 and 90 too). Last of 4 last time out at Newmarket but that was on soft ground and I think he has a big chance here if ready to go after a lay off since August.
Makes Tapeta debut. If he goes on the surface, he has a good chance as he ran 2nd in the Britannia last season. He will come on for his reappearance run last time and drops a pound here.

United Approach is back at Newcastle, where he ran a solid second last summer off a higher mark. He was a fair third at Kempton on return and now drops into a slightly easier race. With that run under his belt and a decent draw, he could be ready to strike.

Winner of this contest last year. It looks more competitive this year but Eldrickjones runs off a mark 3lbs lower and won by 3.5 lengths last year (Zip was second). Been some market interest. Roger Fell has probably been a bit unlucky not to have a recent winner. The six year old is a course specialist with three wins and two seconds at this course. Would benefit from a strong pace to aim at as he stays beyond this trip. Makes seasonal debut (has run well fresh in the past) with the stable coming into form.

Benacre was very impressive when winning very easily over this C&D last time out, which was his first attempt at it. He's been hit by a 6lb higher mark now, which has meant that he's fairly weak in the market. But this C&D clearly suited him, and crucially, he has been competitive off marks as high as his current one in the recent past. He runs off 82 here but started his campaign last year with a place on the AW off 92 and was only beaten a length, so that's a major clue that he could well defy this mark.

A Richard Hannon trained 4-year-old who has had 9 races on the a/w, winning 3 times and has finished in the frame 3 times. His last win was in December in a class 3 at Kempton over 1 mile when leading over 1 furlong out to win by 1 1/2 lengths. He is in a class 3 handicap over 7f and has Tom Marquand in the saddle. This gelding had a race 9 days ago in the flat at Newmarket in a class 2 handicap over 7f on good going when finishing 3rd of the 6 runners, beaten 3 1/2 lengths. He is back on the a/w and has won over this distance. Has a decent e/w shout in this race today.
4yo irish gelding Grand Karat is in great form with form figures of 1314. Should make another step forward here today on 2nd run after a 6 month break. Should be in the mix.
On the basis of the last run, Thunder Roar has the rating and ability to be in the mix at the end. 4 places looks value here.
Showed better form LTO when 3rd of 9 at Redcar last month and does have experience over C&D and just a pound over last winning mark, so should be a contender tomorrow.

Media Shooter won second time up both as a juvenile and last year as a 3-year-old. Having his first start as a 4-year-old following a long layoff, he could go one better and make a winning seasonal debut this year. He posted some good runs in defeat last year, with one of his better efforts being a close 4th on his only start at Newcastle (over 6f) in a class 2 handicap. He finished off last season with a comfortable turf win, in first-time cheekpieces on his first start over this 7f trip. A repeat of that would give him a leading chance here.

Is a 4 time C/D winner who came 2nd in this race last year and recent prep looks like they have been trained with this race in mind to try to go one better. On a decent mark of 83 here, good apprentice back up claiming 5lb and very good trainer who is tops here numerically by some way last 5 seasons, 12 percent with a Lsp of 36.23 on his 4yo plus in same period, making current 18/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Won multiple times last season over a mile and most likely needed the comeback run at Kempton LTO. Jockey claiming 3 lbs, who won on the horse 3 times last season, is back on board, and the stable had a big winner last week at Newmarket. If handling the drop in trip, looks well drawn to give a good account.
I'll chance Jack Channon's Hiromichi after looking tubby and not fit on season debut. But it holds a good strike rate when fit, and the trainer does well here. A good price to aim at.
Cairdeas returns to seven furlongs for all-weather debut but did stay on over six furlongs, and this was the winning trip last season.

Knights Gold has won his last two starts in Class 5 handicaps at Kempton and Leicester last month. He moves up to Class 4 here off a 5lb higher mark, but with the stable in good form and Hollie Doyle riding, he looks a good each way bet with 4 places on offer.
From my MTF notes: BF fifth of 14, left with too much to do entering straight. Kept on well, nearest finish. Note next time out.

FOUR FIFTY This colt makes his handicap debut following a promising victory over this exact course and distance in a novice event, which is always a good sign. The return to seven furlongs is viewed positively by expert observers, and he has landed an excellent draw in stall 2, which is a significant asset here. Being unexposed in handicap company, there's a strong possibility he could be well-treated on his opening mark, making his current odds look rather appealing for a horse with clear potential.

Andalprofit looked seriously sharp when bolting up over 6f here last time and the handicapper’s reacted with a 12lb rise. He steps up to 7f now but if he’s still improving like it looked, he’s got a real shot at going in again.
The fact that this horse remains with the yard despite having a pretty low mark should be a pointer here. Consistent since handicapping.

Too free and probably needed the run last time. Looks well in here as drops 2lb and has an excellent 3lb claimer on top. Narrowly beaten over course and distance off 70 back in October. Runs off a net 69 here. Big chance.

This one has won over 6f here on her 2nd ever run. After a blip next time, she was a good 2nd at Doncaster over 6.5f in class 2. She goes up 4lb, slightly up in trip, but drops 2 grades to class 4. Stall 1 is a poor draw for this course, but if it proves no problem, she could make it 2 for 2 here.
Disappointed going for a hat trick when last seen in February. He was up in grade and 6lb higher and came in last. Been freshened up and worth an each-way bet from the same mark.
Followed two 2nd place finishes with a win at Pontefract in October. Not seen since, but enters handicap company on a competitive mark and holds an each-way chance.

On the hope of needing the run last time out, and at this price, the reward for a place alone outweighs any sense of risk for me. With the best recent run (win) coming on the A/W prior to the last run out, it's definitely worth a second look on the promise of improvement.

Jack Channon is not a frequent visitor to High Gosforth Park, but he sends two here from his Newbury base. Ferrous is on a hat-trick and has a good record on the AW with four wins and a place from just the six runs. Callum Rodriguez is back on board and is 1 from 1 with a 100% record.

GERMANIC showed up well on his seasonal reappearance and stable debut latest. He was regularly aimed high for his former trainer William Haggas and looking feasibly treated in the handicap sphere likely sharper now he could prove hard to contain.

225 days should not put you off. Can go well fresh, so a chance is taken on Telemark, who is a 4-year-old chestnut gelding trained by Simon and Ed Crisford under the Rabbah Racing team. It is on the same competitive mark today with 3 wins and some places so far. With a win strike of approx 30%, it can win.
This looks like a decent 6f handicap at Newcastle. Willem Twee is drawn high, has some decent form over course and distance, and has had 3 races already this year, so should be fighting fit for this.
7yo irish gelding Strike Red is in nice form and he is a two-time C&D. Was a good 2nd of 11 lto over 6f at Leicester and should be in the mix here under Billy Garritty.
Badri ran a bit of a stinker here on penultimate start but left that behind with a not too far away 5th of 13 at Southwell two weeks ago. Races off a pound lower mark today.

Had a very good course profile when with A. Balding, including a win in very hot class 2 handicap. Not reached that level for current connections, but is very well handicapped here off today's mark of 98. Very good jockey trainer combination makes current 14/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Has been running well in Bahrain when two wins and two seconds from his last four starts following a break of almost four months off. Had wind surgery and was gelded during the break. Yard & jockey both in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

Looks at the pace angle in the race and has won a couple of Class 2, 6-furlong handicaps on turf. Comfortable course and distance winner in a lower grade last year. If transferring the best of his turf form, he should be competitive. The underlying form of the yard is decent, and they go well at the track.

Ferrous has an obvious claim to follow up his recent successes, but I'm looking down the card for some juicier prices. Up until his last run, Westmorian looked unstoppable, so if we overlook that Southwell flop, he's a contender to be in the mix at the line. The trainer is putting the claimer up on board to take off 5 lbs. GL.

Korker’s better than he showed at Southwell last time and comes back to Newcastle, where he’s run well before. He’s got strong sprint form in the book and if he’s back on song, he could easily get involved.

This looks very open, and Bosh at 14/1 is the selection. He has dropped to a very good-looking mark, and a couple of recent runs will have him spot on. He goes well on the all-weather and was largely consistent in the same grade last season off higher marks.

Ex-Irish trained 4yo. Respectable UK debut run at the start of the month after 8 months off the track. Can improve for the run, a good low draw for this 5f dash, a 2lb lower mark now, and he has a strong jockey change. Three runs back, he was only beaten 2L on fast ground, in a 13-runner handicap, against much stronger rivals than what he now faces.

Respectable return run from the 7-year-old last month, despite the inexperienced jockey making a mess of things at the start. A good replacement jockey takes over in the saddle, who got a nice tune out of the selection last summer. Two wins and two very near misses, the last of those runs was off a 5lb higher mark. Every chance in this company off his current mark.

Lightly raced 4yo, 3 wins from 10 on turf, including over this 6f C/D. You could forgive his run four weeks ago, after coming off an 8-month break and on unsuitable slow ground, and he will be happier back on this g/f surface. Beaten just a length on his final start last year, in a 16-runner, £39K class 2 handicap. He can be a player in this £9K class 3 handicap, and he has a 2lb lower mark now.

Top Irish stable, smart 2-year-old form, runner-up twice, 2nd in the Futurity at Doncaster and 2 wins. Won the Group 3 Autumn Stakes at Newmarket, showed it had trained on when winning over C/D after a 5-month break. Beat Lambourn, winner of the Chester Vase last time out. Cannot oppose.

Current form of 2-1-2 makes Acapulco Bay a very promising 3-year-old bay colt. Trained by Aidan O'Brien, with 3 runs, 2 seconds, and a win, puts the win rate at approximately 33%. So, a chance to win or place again today against the favorite.

Won a weak Group 1 on his final start last year in France but had previously chased home Hotazhell, who is well fancied in today's French Guineas. The favourite looks tough to beat, but he's the main danger if trained on from last year.
Ballydoyle runner who is well in at the weights here. Strong finish to last season winning final two races at this course in group two and three company.
Can definitely win this on today's terms, especially if Diego Valasquez needs the run. Would have to reverse form with Lord Masseus, but has the run under belt now.

Took a while to get going last time when beating Mutasarref (reopposes today) by a neck here a month ago. Mutasarref was getting 2lb that day and they are on level weights today. The race conditions were very similar to today: 1m, good ground, small field, and Lord Massusus was always going to beat Mutasarref once he got balanced in the straight, so I don't think the 2lb swing will make any difference. Diego Velazquez is the hot favorite (around 4/6). He struggled in top Group 1 races last year over slightly longer trips and finished the season winning a Group 2 and a Group 3 over 1m and 1m1f. He's dropping down to this Listed race and clearly is the horse to beat. This will be his first run of the season and he may not be fully wound up.

A big price but worth a small punt on this gelding. He won over 1m last season but then was given a campaign over 7f and not disgraced in many of his races. He started his 4yo career over 6f early April but appeared to want more furlongs. The trainer has truly obliged with a return to this trip, which he won at last season.
Smart Sort, who hit the frame at the top level last year, notably when placed in the French Guineas, made a fair return last month and should be hard to beat if building on that.

Won a maiden over 6f at Fairyhouse on second career start last June and improved greatly as the season progressed finishing second in a Group 3 at the Curragh in September before ending the season with a close 4th at the Breeders Cup. Will improve again this season and a leading contender.
Lightly-raced winner. C&D winner. 6¼ lengths seventh of 11 to Atsila in Athasi Stakes (3/1) at the Curragh (8f, good) 6 days ago. Hood on 1st time and she's a live each-way candidate.

6yo irish mare Veras Secret has won a hot hc here at this course over 1m last September. Soft ground lto didn't suit and she will be happy to be back here at this course and on faster ground. Should be in the mix.

This one improved considerably from debut over 7f on soft to finish 2nd over 8f on the A/W and dropped to 7f on turf. Won on fast going the last two for this team. This demands a fair bit more, but she is improving and the trainer's horses cannot be ignored, so worth the E/W at 20/1.

Sweet Chariot could be an improver as a three-year-old. Despite being a low-rated handicapper as a two-year-old, she finished by breaking her maiden tag off a mark of 73 in a six-furlong handicap. She started off this season finishing well into 2nd of 15 in a seven-furlong handicap at the Curragh off a mark of 80. She could sneak at least a place, making the big jump into Group 3 company over a mile.
Take an EW chance on 3yo irish filly Easy Mover. She should be much sharper today on her 2nd run after a 8 month break. Holds every chance to be in the mix here.

Top Irish stable, smart on the flat and over hurdles. Jumping not perfect on his chase debut but still beat Encanto Bruno comfortably. Recorded an RPR of 147, will improve for that experience. Cannot oppose.

Has about a stone to find on hurdles form, but the favorite looked far from being a natural over fences when winning on Chase debut last time. I would rather chance the selection who was running over an inadequate trip on his Chase debut last time and will improve for the step up in trip here.

Etawa looks primed for a breakthrough win in the 16:05 Fillies Maiden at Leopardstown. Trained by Dermot Weld and ridden by C.D. Hayes, she caught the eye on debut when staying on strongly for third over the same 1m2f trip. That effort suggested she'll come on significantly for the run, especially with experience under her belt. With a strong pedigree, sired by Kingman out of Etneya, and a race that lacks depth, Etawa has every right to improve past her rivals. Butterfly Wings, who finished behind her last time, reopposes but may struggle to reverse the form. Expect Etawa to progress and deliver. Bonne chance.

Highly promising daughter of Justify & Butterflies ( Dam's sire Galileo ) who is thrice raced was last seen over this course and distance 32 days ago where finishing a respectable 4th/7 that was her return run after a 237 day break and she is entitled to strip fitter and be a lot sharper at the finish this time out A P O'brien's inmate is open to plenty of progress especially now as a 3yo and she did look better built last time out as that was also the first time she was seen racing as a 3yo and she is likely to be a whole different proposition this season this looks to be a straightforward assignment for Butterfly Wings and she can put this fillies maiden straight to bed before moving onto better things the tongue strap is also applied for the first time here jockey W M Lordon takes the ride and can give Butterfly Wings a promising ride here at Leopardstown expect to see this good looking filly with the big white face thundering home . Respected .
Once-raced filly. Second of 5 in maiden at Dundalk (10.7f, 15/2) on debut 37 days ago. Open to improvement and could go well.

Twice a winner on the flat when trained in France, who did not show much in the first 3 starts in maiden hurdles for Willie Mullins, but showed huge improvement the first time in a handicap when won with any amount in hand at Fairyhouse last month. Carries a 13 lbs penalty for that effort but finished powerfully and looks on the improve and could be useful.

CSW back on top after selection was an unlucky loser 3 runs back with CSW on top, falling 2 out when going well and looking a likeky winner. 8lb better off with fav for 1.5l defeat on penultimate start . big chance

BATMAN GIRAC remains lightly-raced previously aimed higher and he now gets to take his chance from a joint career-low handicap mark. He seems suited by quick NH turf and representing high-profile owners and the top trainer he should be competitive in this company.

3 wins in the last 4, the latest off the back of a break, so no need to worry from that angle. Distance looks to be spot on and looks a good opportunity to make it 2 from 2 after fairly breezing the last run out.
First Dare fell last time out over hurdles. If that is a blip, then the horse can be forgiven. Will appreciate this trip and will go well on this type of ground. Looks over-priced.

Frankendael is a 6-year-old bay gelding trained by Eric McNamara in Ireland. Frankendael began his career on the Flat in the UK with 2 wins from 9 starts. Under the training of Eric McNamara, he has developed into a competitive hurdler, and you can forgive his last pulled-up race here.

Has yet to get off the mark but is the top speed-rated horse in the lineup and was placed over hurdles 3 and 4 starts back (11st 4lb - 11st 8lb), including at this course. This race represents a big step up in class on its handicap debut, but this Milan gelding carries its lowest weight to date by far of 9st 12lb (previous lowest 10st 13lb). Has a long break to overcome, but the trainer is showing a £84.50 profit with hurdlers running after a break. Could go well off a low weight today at big odds (18/1 best price).
Likely improver now going handicapping. Has been ridden with handicaps in mind, and his opening mark of 116 looks appealing as his flat mark is 81. Certainly of each-way interest.
Good run on debut when 4th, and considering finished very strongly there, this upping of trip is a good move. Top bet.
Dabashan showed plenty of promise on debut. Will have learned plenty from that run and can be expected to go close today.
Better ground today and a trip that should suit better. This horse is a lot better than what we have seen so far and has some good entries, so will need to start winning soon.
If we take into account primarily the results shown earlier in the season, it is worth highlighting Vorfreude, who was twice second in the two April races at Navan.

Was plenty short enough in betting market on debut run, but was far too green in running to do themselves justice, when coming 6/18 beaten 14.5 lengths in a decent maiden over extended 1.2 miles @ Cork. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, better ground here should suit, step up to this 1.4 miles a plus and top jockey/trainer combination makes current 7.50 very good Ew value in the race.
Not expected on debut last time. Missed the break and made late progress. Steps up in trip here, which on breeding will suit. Worth an each-way bet.
3rd on both outings but sets the form standard in this, and if improving more as expected, can go and win this. Good bet.

Esherann is a 3-year-old colt trained by D K Weld. He makes a belated debut and is a well-named colt from a dam called Eshera (IRE), who only ran three times, finishing 2-1-1, the latter in a listed race. Both wins came on today's good ground. D K Weld also has an excellent record with debutantes, with 73 wins from the last 243 runners if sent off at 9-2 or less. This colt, who is related to three individual winners, notably Erzindjan, rated as high as 106 and also trained by D K Weld, should play a big part in proceedings.

Was well beaten over 6f on debut at the Curragh in August last year but improved to finish just outside the places in fourth when stepped up to today's trip at Dundalk last month when returning from eight months off. Should be fitter today. Was gelded during the break. Should be involved at the finish.

SCARLET RAIDER could be an interesting outsider for a powerful dual-purpose yard. A three year old with a pedigree which could be better suited to all-weatrher racing , but this does not look the strongest of races and maybe connections are looking for him to break his maiden giving confidence fo his journey ahead.
Disappointed when only 9th of 12 at Naas on debut in August. Not seen since and should be better than that. Each way chance if finding some improvement.

The model I run suggests Day Trader can win this Killarney opener. The model simulated this race and had Day Trader in first, Young Churchil in second, and Woodview Lad in third. This result has largely been driven by Day Trader having the second highest RPR of the field. He also has the joint highest Top Speed on this card. A good second in Down Royal last week and looks to go one better here over the same distance.
The run last time when 2nd has been franked and is still progressing. Should have a very good chance in this here.
Well-related newcomer Dam had one race in a bumper but is a half-sister to Commanche Red, who was a smart hurdler. Gordon Elliot has a reasonable record in this type of race and could go well.

Elusive Ogie could be one who runs well from an each-way point of view, good odds. This horse has a bit more experience over hurdles compared to a few of these opponents, that experience may be an advantage. Not a bad run last time out over hurdles, finished 5th of 14 when he wasn't really fancied at the odds but he didn't do badly, could do similar again today. Ground conditions won't be as soft as last time, today's better ground conditions may be more suitable.

Romany Brown goes in search of a maiden win here and has been constantly knocking on the door of late with a runner-up finish as well as three 3rd placed finishes inside the last handful of outings. A win is around the corner given those performances and near misses.
Hasn't been far away in the last 3 efforts, and with betting in favor, worth a look on hurdles debut. A decent chance to get the top spot off the back of those decent bumper runs.
Useful flat performer who has placed in group races in Germany and Italy. Makes hurdles debut having run once on the flat for this yard. Likely to be there or thereabouts if taking to hurdling.
Showed promise in the first two starts but has since found it difficult. Comes here fresh which could see an improvement on most recent form. Good jockey booking will help this one's chances.

Went off joint favorite on race debut in a bumper over 2 miles at Navan on soft ground back in March. Raced prominently but did not get home, weakening out of it 2 from home. Should have benefited from the experience and could do better now in a maiden hurdle on better ground.
Steps up in trip today after a promising 3rd last time out. Looks on a good mark. Stable going well this season. Ground will suit. Jockey claiming 7lb will help.
Showed some promise in both starts over hurdles and was placed at Limerick when last seen in January last year. Long absence to overcome, but has an each-way chance if retaining that ability.

Paggane represents the stable of W P Mullins. She is ahead of her rivals in this race by the main indicators. However, it's worth noting that her main wins have been in hurdles races, so the odds from the bookies aren't that low either. Paul Townend will be in the saddle today

A 6-time hurdle winner who won a beginner's chase easily last time out over 2m6f at Kilbeggan. Stays this longer trip well and is very well handicapped over fences in comparison to his hurdles mark, so a big run looks on the cards today.

Has gone up 7 lb to a mark of 120, its highest so far for a comfortable enough first chase win at Down Royal over this distance (€7k) last time out carrying 11 st 1 lb. Is up 4 notches in class but carries its lowest chase weight to date of 9 st 11 lb (11 st 1 lb) and was placed in a €48k hurdles race last April. Is on the up over fences, so may well be able to follow up in this lot tougher race off a low weight.

It’s a bit surprising to see Padraig Roche’s 7-year-old gelding BRAZIL still flying under the radar, especially after his eye-catching effort in the Ulster National at Downpatrick 42 days ago. This son of GALILEO, once a Cheltenham Festival hero after toppling Willie Mullins' highly-touted Gaelic Warrior in the 2022 Boodles, showed real grit over a marathon 29-furlong trip, finishing a close-up fourth just a head shy of third. Once rated 144 over hurdles, This charge now finds himself off a much-reduced chase mark of 120 a staggering 24lb drop. It’s fair to say he hasn’t had the smoothest transition to chasing, but that Downpatrick run suggested he may finally be turning the corner. Now, with a 1lb drop in the weights and a more manageable trip on the cards, conditions seem right for a bold showing. Another big plus is the continued presence of Mark Walsh, whose current 45.16% place strike rate over the past month, coupled with a strong 37.14% place strike rate at Killarney, adds serious confidence. With all things considered, it’s surprising Brazil isn’t a single-figure price in the market. At 12/1, he looks a very appealing each-way play.

Moonovercloon was going well when falling in the Irish National and the better going here at Killarney should better suit his stamina limitations and he should at least get a place with a clear round.
Twice a winner over fences this year but was pulled up last time at Punchestown in what was a hat-trick attempt. Holds an each-way chance.

This is the trainer's only entry he's got out today, as the owner has got 4 entered in this race. They have got the same 3lbs claimer on board, as this is his only ride of the day. A good value each-way bet for the 4 places available.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is each way on Gaelic Arc. This is a large price and so still offers value each way. There are 4 places on offer at B365 for this race. Gaelic Arc lacks form here, but does step out with the highest RPR and therefore has shown potential before. Carries towards the lower end of those weights given the lack of form, and has won at this course before (although a while ago admittedly). Tested now at this longer 3m distance, which represents a step up in trip. Over longer distances, these weight differentials statistically prove to be more important. The total weight differential to the top of the market is close to 1 stone.

13 lengths beaten in 5th place here last year but carrying 5 lbs less and with a useful 5 lb claimer taking off 5 lbs too. Has proven ability beyond 3 miles and looks the most interesting at bigger prices.
Donkey Years returns after a 135-day break. This is competitive, but he is reasonably handicapped and has a chance to squeeze into the frame based on his previous form. Each way hopeful.

Birdie Or Bust finished 3rd at the Cheltenham Festival Grade 2 Ryanair Mares Novice Hurdle in 2024 but has not got close to winning any of her three attempts in novice chases this season over two miles, being beaten ten lengths in her first two and well down the field last time at Thurles in February. This looks easier for her after a break, going up in distance to two and a half miles.

Out For A Stroll is a 4-year-old filly trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien. She is lightly raced over hurdles, winning once. However, her last win came on the flat at Limerick, so she's quite versatile. Today, she's oddly sent chasing, which is quite young for a 4-year-old, but she has ability. In receipt of all the weight allowances, she can be a big contender, receiving 15lb from the favorite Birdie Or Bust who hasn't set the world alight since she has been sent chasing . In addition, Joseph Patrick O'Brien targets this meeting and is 36/141 winners, showing a healthy LSP of £43.04.
Galileo Sand has run twice with credit to finish 3rd and 4th in March and just 11 days ago. J P O'Brien runs two in this race, but Galileo Sand has to be the favorite of the two with his experience.
Patrick Mullins has been given the steering job by Joseph Patrick O'Brien, which could see this son of Caravaggio making his debut a winning one.

LE DIABLO runs for a small but clearly shrewd Irish yard who are 2/7 with their Bumper runners at this venue. That clearly reads well as does the booking of Harry Swan among the winners recently , so there are reasons to expect a big run from this young horse second-up having been punted on debut.
Power Of Words did well on hurdle debut at Fairyhouse last month, placing 4th of 21. He is now making his flat debut and could do well and get into the frame.
First run since leaving John Patrick Murtagh when fourteenth of 16 in handicap at Limerick (8.2f, heavy) 16 days ago. Back up in trip. Needs a couple of these to falter.

Serial winner on different going, back to a shorter trip and winner at this venue already. A smaller field could all be the ticket to getting home in front once again off the back of a 'blip' run last time out, only managing 8th.

Stable debut having been gelded and would have a decent chance on his previous winning form when sluicing up by 5L+ back in January on AW. He ran to a mark exceeding the one he runs off today, so is worth each-way consideration.

Lady Lunette is a 5-year-old bay mare trained by RP Cody and ridden by Cohen today. Forgive the last run as it was the first after a layoff. This horse is a course winner, so the potential is definitely there.

Has yet to score on turf but has a win at Dundalk under its belt (last year) and was only beaten by a head at Fairyhouse 5 starts back. This will be its toughest handicap to date, but it does carry its lowest weight to date of 8st 3lb (9st previous lowest). Plus, it's top 3 speed rated and joint top rated in some quarters, all of which could see it get off the mark on turf today at big odds (18/1 best price) with a step up to 10f likely to suit.

San Andreas, a seasoned nine-year-old gelding trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien, is set to compete in the Leopardstown Golf and Driving Range Handicap over 1 mile 2 furlongs. The race features a competitive field of 16 runners and offers a prize fund of €15,000. San Andreas has demonstrated consistent form on the All-Weather circuit, with multiple victories and placings at Dundalk. Notably, he secured back-to-back wins over 1m 2f and 1m 4f in December 2024. While his recent turf performances have been less prominent, his experience and adaptability make him a formidable contender.

Jungle Cove was 18th of 19 in a charity race here a week ago. That was over two miles, and he will have benefited from the outing. He is now being dropped in trip, which should suit and could possibly outrun his odds.

Palmezzano looks progressive after a strong runner-up effort last time out, showing promise over a similar trip. He's trained by Joseph O'Brien, a master at placing his 3-year-olds well in handicaps. With Dylan Browne McMonagle on board, who rides this track exceptionally well, and a handy draw (stall 3), everything points to a big run. He's on the upgrade and could go one better today.

Mister Adam makes his handicap debut after 3 unplaced efforts over shorter in maiden company. He was 3rd of 18 at Curragh on his last start in March. That was over 8 furlongs, but with today's 12 furlongs sure to suit, he looks a good each-way bet.
NUIT has hinted at ability over 1m and 1m1f in maiden company. Makes handicap debut with potential to step forward from previous runs.
Lightly-raced winner. 1 win from 1 run this year. 12/1, career best when winning 7-runner handicap at Dundalk (10.7f) 30 days ago, driven out. Expected to be bang there.

Berto Ramirez is a 3-year-old gelding trained by David Marnane. He was sent off as short as 3-1 on his AW handicap debut last time out at Dundalk over 10.5f, beaten 2.25 lengths under today's jockey, Luke McAteer. He didn't get much luck in running, and today's step up to 12f should suit him, being out of German Derby winner Sea The Moon. He also brings course form to the table, finishing 8/16 over short and the 6/18 Birdie Time RPR of 64, a 1/2 length ahead, has since won, posting an RPR of 81. He has also finished 2/18 at this track over 7f last August on todays good ground, and Berto Ramirez should have some wiggle room off today's mark of 77.

Junkyard Dog represents the stable of Joseph Patrick O'Brien. He has made a great start to this season, winning a tough 20 entrants race at Navan. Today's good ground should suit him. The chances of a podium are good

A J Bolger entry, a 3-year-old yet to place but bred to race over further than has so far, has got the correct distance here and now takes handicap debut sporting headgear. May improve if returning fit.

The Danny Feeling is a 5-year-old son of Diamond Boy ex Feeling Flemish from the family of Synchronised by Sadler's Wells. Last time out, he was third at 13/2 behind Concannon 8/11f by Berkshire at Galway last October. That bumper has produced two winners from two runners. He reappears here in this 2m1 bumper for lady riders where he'll be ridden by Miss J Townend (who won this race last season on Jump Allen 11/10 by Manduro) for T O'Brien. I think he may open his account here, and I make him my Nap of the day.
